clue.text: Snip off its tail and this pest is no more

parts.note: something that is no more only was, so the past tense stands in

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, here taken from the word Snip

explanation.surface: Cut the tail off an insect and it is dead and gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures killing an insect; really, cutting the tail letter from the answer leaves a word meaning 'is no more'.
explanation.definitionFit: This stinging insect is a familiar summer nuisance, hence a pest.

clue.text: See parts wound round wrist

parts.note: to see is to watch

indicators.note: wound, as in twisted round, signals the letters of parts are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for fitting components wrapped around the wrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as an injury but means twisted, signalling the anagram; the definition is the descriptive phrase 'round wrist', saying where the band sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The band holding a timepiece sits around the wearer's wrist, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: Slow mover reaching Pole, in voyage

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for Pole inside the word for a voyage

parts.note: to sail is to make a voyage; a sail is a trip by boat
N stands for the North Pole

explanation.surface: An explorer creeping slowly towards the Pole on a long journey.
explanation.definitionFit: This shelled garden creature is a byword for creeping slowness.

clue.text: With this sort of name, no telling who your. mother was

definitions.text: With this sort of name, no telling who your. mother was

parts.words: With this sort of name, no telling who your. mother was
parts.note: a surname built from the father's name, like Johnson, records only the paternal line, so the mother goes unmentioned

explanation.surface: A remark about a name that reveals nothing about one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A name formed from the father's forename records paternity only, leaving maternity unrecorded.

clue.text: Provide assistance covering any puzzle set aside

indicators.note: covering means the word for assisting wraps round the scrambled letters

parts.note: to abet is to provide assistance

indicators.note: to puzzle is to confuse, so the letters of any are jumbled

explanation.surface: Helping with a puzzle that has been shelved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzle' looks like a noun (the crossword itself) but is a verb meaning confuse, so it jumbles the letters inside the word for assisting, which 'covering' wraps round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in abeyance is suspended or shelved, temporarily laid aside.

clue.text: Role sailor takes in uprising-due to gin, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the letters from the bottom up, turning the whole run

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's part in a mutiny, blamed on drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in uprising' turns PARTTAR into RATTRAP. A gin here is not the spirit but a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching animals, and a rodent snare is one example.

clue.text: Word that's always contradicted

parts.note: read as the word that is the opposite of 'always', not a word forever being disputed

explanation.surface: A statement that is forever being disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning at no time is the direct opposite of always.

clue.text: Clear love declaration

parts.note: manifest means clear or obvious
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A plain statement of one's love.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's published statement of policy is a public declaration.

clue.text: Many cry in Spain for the king

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
ole is the Spanish shout of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: Crowds in Spain shouting for their monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is Old King Cole, the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme monarch is known as Old King Cole.

clue.text: Space traveller interfered with radio set

indicators.note: something interfered with is tampered with and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tampered with a wireless set.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet orbiting the sun travels through space.

clue.text: Suitably prepared entrant is certain to pass

indicators.note: letters suitably prepared are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A well-prepared exam candidate is sure to succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like passing an exam; here it means passing away, fading.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting or short-lived is bound to go by quickly.

clue.text: Girl put on some ny-lens-synthetic material

parts.note: Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A woman puts on a pair of nylons made of man-made fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: This plastic, used for records and flooring, is a synthetic substance.

clue.text: Draw, to obtain about a pound.

indicators.note: about means the word for obtain goes around the pound sign

parts.note: to have something is to obtain it
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra)

explanation.surface: A tie that earns roughly a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a hole is halved when both sides take the same score, i.e. it is drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, sharing a hole with equal scores means drawing it.

clue.text: The skill needed by its skipper

definitions.text: The skill needed by its skipper

parts.words: The skill needed by its skipper
parts.note: split the answer into two words: the craft of the air, the skill a pilot needs

explanation.surface: A question about what skill a ship's captain needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane's pilot needs mastery of flying, the skill of the skies.

clue.text: Flora of Gibraltar?

parts.note: Gibraltar is known as the Rock, so its flora would be vegetation of the Rock

explanation.surface: A question about the plants growing on Gibraltar.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine species growing among stones are named after the stony ground they favour.

clue.text: Eviction from assembly

definitions.meaning: throwing someone out of their home
the number of people who come to a gathering

explanation.surface: Being thrown out of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both an ejection and the attendance at an event.

clue.text: Catch you'd learn easily

parts.note: a catch is a round sung in parts; a simple song with refrain is easily learnt

explanation.surface: A trick you could pick up without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: A catch is a round for several voices; this kind is a short song with a recurring refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: A short song with a refrain repeated over and over is a simple tune to pick up.

clue.text: Cap is adjusted in this way by the artist

indicators.note: letters adjusted are moved around into a new order

parts.note: so means thus or in this way

explanation.surface: A painter tilts his beret just so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' suggests straightening a beret, but it signals reshuffling the letters of 'Cap is'; 'by' merely links the wordplay to the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish painter who founded Cubism is a famous artist.

clue.text: Fish-slice once used to protect a man

definitions.text: once used to protect a man

parts.note: cod is a fish
a piece is a slice

explanation.surface: A kitchen fish slice once used as armour.
explanation.definitionFit: This pouch at the front of old breeches covered and protected a man's groin.

clue.text: In two parts, in the manner set out below

parts.note: as means in the manner of
under means below, as in 'as set out under'

explanation.surface: A document divided in two, as described further down.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn apart means split into separate pieces.

clue.text: Setting forth, will be turning up after the others, in the Channel isles

indicators.note: in puts the island abbreviation inside the turned word
in a down clue turning up reads the word from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: coming after the others is coming later
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Someone arriving late on Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be turning up' is a down-clue reversal; 'after the others' is a definition-by-description of later. 'Setting forth' means narrating, as a recital of facts does.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed account or narration is a setting forth of facts.

clue.text: Stuff to cut in the field

parts.note: to pad is to stuff
to dock is to cut short

explanation.surface: Fodder to be mown in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A small enclosed grassy area for horses is a field.

clue.text: Grazing land beyond the river

parts.note: past means beyond
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Fields for cattle on the far side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass-covered fields where livestock feed are grazing land.

clue.text: Goes ahead with the loans

definitions.meaning: sums of money lent in advance

explanation.surface: Proceeds with the borrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both moves forward and payments lent up front.

clue.text: Letter bringing complaint, following article

indicators.note: following means the complaint comes after the article

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
an itch is a minor ailment or complaint

explanation.surface: A letter of grievance arriving after a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence; it is the name of a letter of the alphabet, H.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet is a letter.

clue.text: One policeman to join the Spanish force

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP stands for military police, i.e. a military policeman
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A lone officer joining Spain's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or urge someone on is to force them.

clue.text: Exercise with first mate and cause some annoyance

parts.note: PE is physical education, i.e. exercise
Eve was Adam's mate, the first woman

explanation.surface: A workout with the chief officer that proves irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: To irk or vex someone is to annoy them.

clue.text: Welshman's platform

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name
the possessive ending supplies an S

explanation.surface: A stage belonging to a man from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stage at one end of a hall is a platform.

clue.text: Give a ring back

indicators.note: back means the word for ring is read in reverse

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell

explanation.surface: Phone someone in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a ring back' reads as returning a phone call; 'back' actually turns the bell-ringing verb round, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate or assign a share is to give it out.

clue.text: Police club

parts.note: read as the weapon a constable carries, not a social club for officers

explanation.surface: A social society for officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable's short heavy baton is a club carried by the police.

clue.text: Bottomless pit a feature of these 'islands

definitions.text: Bottomless pit a feature of these 'islands

parts.words: Bottomless pit a feature of these 'islands
parts.note: the place of damnation, the bottomless pit, appears as letters in the middle of the island group's name

explanation.surface: A remark that some islands contain an abyss.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian Ocean archipelago is a group of islands.

clue.text: Forms of worship

parts.note: forms are benches, so these are the long seats in a church

explanation.surface: Kinds of religious practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Long wooden benches in a church are forms used during worship.
